## Design

### 2026-10-09 – Well, today was a crazy one.

**7h**

Well, today was a crazy one.

I decided to restart week 1 to pursue my own project for two major reasons:
1. The Starbie Project wouldn't have given me enough hours to complete the week
2. By doing my own project, I can learn more about the design process and I get gain a better understanding.

So, I created a new repository and KiCad project for the new project: AmbiSense. It's a portable environment sensor that has capabilities to sense external light levels, sound levels, humidity, and temperature.

And so, with a fresh start came a new README.md and blank schematic

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 135113](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/f8ac38b2c85d25b0b5f5c1a8ec7c86f5cb6303409c50bd4e014348678ff98323.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 140042](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/b3db0bd330d781f03df66bfff9e3c9431da2996a1fe713b33400ba7535284053.png)

The next steps I had to take were... interesting. I had to select and find the parts I wanted to use in order to make this thing real, and found a couple places to look, those being DigiKey, Octopart, and SnapMagic.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 140337](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/0d5c63d38f80d7a0f758ac649a11ec18da9d3cd072d0cca24a8aa8a92eca0c61.png)

The first step of course was choosing the brain of this operation, and I settled on the ESP32-S2. It has lots of pins, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth capabilities, and more. It was perfect. After some searching, I also found a pin layout and datasheet for it that would help me know where to connect things. Data sheets I also used for almost every other new component to tell me what to connect to where and whether it needed something like a resistor or capacitor.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 141224](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/308b8ea15f733a7d8b9b53a42872d24b5a654dae2ddc3f174fbe8a8940e7dabd.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 142856](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/2498ac62171b334e73fa91a176ad604e0464b81fd252cb1da4a9f244a502a709.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 143535](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/50049c3d9dd3dbdf29e51175fc40766814c32e7bc7461def3168c2c8cfeb717f.png)

Once I chose the microcontroller, I found it in the KiCad library and placed it.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 143836](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/23d365bbb287f38f526157c4343e3c855d1373114d26402f207240df1ff3594d.png)

I started with something simple next: The light sensor. For this, I chose to use a light dependent resistor and hooked it up in accordance to some diagrams I found, and I used net labels to help with organizing.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 152813](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/c16c092d8a7e5889e695c665eb623d8c3bed04866ffacae0f6432bc5367b011a.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 152925](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/a545d11ca7a7f3b7771f510c6e44655aad3ee0325aeb2a11eeabaeed6ca63f76.png)

I moved on to a dual-purpose sensor for temperature and humidity. In hindsight, it would have been smart to just use the same one as the Starbie, but too late. Plus, why not go big or go home right? Anyways, same process as the LDR.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 154002](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/456032c35c61db7351d25f1594d2503e992f47f1ff5c36a33645faad7be74dbd.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 154012](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/77c55ef51d8d3e36bf170296b57b48822adc7a09fedaf410a9b020210dd6a234.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 154718](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/f08a013ce45a2f10ecbb2f0344d569f74ecb5e56462fffcbdcbca998e0ad27a5.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 154822](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/ca0f004498e90cbadd7f6be9fd0bf07d821bf351580124266397b14e4d66b5b8.png)

The next part took the better part of this session. I wanted to incorporate a rechargeability feature, which was much more complicated than I thought. I needed to wire in a USB-C receiver, which already had tons of pins to connect, some of which I didn't even see on my microcontroller at first.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 163841](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/26e2c7cfbc9b64b158549b969b34f628466f8b34279c0ba774cd4bd325b58b47.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 163937](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/c641843b5ae55b083209dabfa6a292d89139dad819deaa2b8129db48353ba273.png)

It was around now that I decided to look into my microcontroller a little more and I discovered that the ESP32-S2 wasn't in stock almost anywhere. So, I pivoted. I decided on a little upgrade and went for the ESP32-S3-MINI-1. It has even more pins, and clearer documentation, plus it was in stock. Being from the same family I didn't have to change all that much, although I did have to import my own symbol for it that I found on SnapMagic.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 163937](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/c641843b5ae55b083209dabfa6a292d89139dad819deaa2b8129db48353ba273.png)

After that was sorted out, I started on the power system again. Over the course of many hours, I searched for datasheets and wired in receivers, sockets, converters, and chargers. Although it was stupid complicated, there was lots of documentation from Texas Instruments who produced the most complicated parts, so in the end I was able to have it wired correctly (I think) and even have power and charging indications routed to the ESP32 for later usage.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 170949](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/93c14a92c6e5bdf6165f2af30831a7b9547bad645de677f0a4872adc618c3630.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 174743](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/87c5226b88c27596966ae3b2c21a870c0ff48112b516773c41b5cc1c79a2e802.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 194337](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/c985663efffa41fea9d4cd3ca3585f2d38ad533bd1b0ce5977a6b273c630075d.png)

To wrap up the session, I decided to go a little bit easier. I set up the OLED and buttons using the Starbie guide and used some footprints from the starter pack as I expect I'll just use the same ones. I also wired up a sound sensor. It has 3 I/O connections, but with the low pin count, it was actually pretty easier to wire in. I expect that the coding portion will be much more difficult and tedious.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 194355](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/023dc4bfb5d6a1c056afa605fbedbcbb476a341743b3f0f8751122a2bc531054.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 200320](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/ac1cce5d1803217342a4247cd0403f5e5970b66f069c846358fc92106246c598.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 200706](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/f7538d641cbdb2b60d9c55208ee97e5d99f38bd0408cb7399fc7d55dff45da56.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 201114](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/8401b94469b1a79861e21d04edd182a8a90cf3e296ef0c92f6bcb8a75eeccad9.png)

And with that, a long long long session was complete. Now I know that datasheets are one's best friend when it comes to new components, and I am just a bit better at wiring I think. Next steps are to make it into a PCB and potentially add another sensor or connectivity device if I find the time and use for one.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 201126](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/45884a1e5c40f17a2c91c77bb191e4632b4c050556e3b5d2f6914ed5eb1ec307.png)
